transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I just keep feeling like I've completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage recently, and I just feel like it was a mistake. Like, every time I mess up an order at work or drop a plate, it just proves that I'm useless. I just feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me because of it.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once liked?

No, I don't think so. I still enjoy the things I usually do when I have some downtime from the restaurant. I haven't really lost interest in them... it's just hard to relax sometimes with everything on my mind. But no, I still like doing my normal stuff.
Have you been feeling down or experiencing a low mood most days, even when you're not thinking about work or the mortgage?

Yeah, I have. Most days, actually. It's like... there's just this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. Even if I'm not actively worrying about the mortgage or messing up, it's still there. I'm just going through the motions at the restaurant, carrying plates and smiling at people because I'm supposed to for the job, not because I actually feel anything good. It's just a really heavy feeling most of the time.
Have you been feeling fatigued or like you don’t have energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally taxing?

No, not really. I mean, I get tired from work, sure... being on my feet all day carrying trays definitely takes it out of you. But if it's my day off and I haven't done much, I don't feel completely drained or anything like that. My energy levels are pretty normal.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety more often than not?

Yeah, actually. My coworkers have pointed it out. Sometimes I get really restless... like, I'll just pace around the restaurant, checking the same tables and looking over the same receipts over and over again. But then other times, it's the exact opposite. I get so slowed down that just grabbing menus and walking over to the POS system takes me way longer than it normally should. So, yeah, it kind of goes back and forth.
Have you been feeling unusually guilty about things, or blaming yourself for things that aren’t really your fault?

Yeah, I have. Actually, that's a big part of why I came in to see someone. I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It weighs on me a lot. And then at work, if I make even a small mistake, it just... it feels like it proves that I’m useless. It makes me feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me.
Have you noticed any days where you don't take pleasure in things you normally enjoy, or where you just feel numb, even when you're not thinking about your worries?

Yeah, most days are like that, actually. There's just this... this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like I'm just going through the motions. I'll be at work carrying plates, smiling at customers, doing all the things I'm supposed to do, but I'm not feeling anything good. It's just numb.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or more than usual, or losing or gaining a noticeable amount of weight?

Yeah, my eating has been pretty all over the place lately. Some weeks I... I barely even touch the staff meal at work. I just don't have any appetite for it. But then other nights, I'll get home from a shift and just eat whatever's in the kitchen, mostly just to feel settled, I guess. So it really goes back and forth.
How long have you been feeling this way — this heavy, empty feeling and the guilt about the mortgage and work mistakes?
Well, the whole thing... this heavy feeling, the guilt, all of it... it's been going on for a while. I'd say the really low, depressed periods have been happening for about a year and two months now.
Before this past year, have you ever had a period of time where you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced other emotional changes that lasted for several weeks or more?

No, I don't think so. I mean, not that I can remember. It really just started getting bad about a year or so ago. Before that, things were mostly fine. I didn't have these long stretches of feeling this empty.

Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or irritable, where you were doing or saying a lot more than usual, or where you needed much less sleep but still had lots of energy?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I've never felt unusually high or energetic. Honestly, it's mostly just been the opposite—feeling really weighed down and tired. I definitely haven't had times where I didn't need sleep or had extra energy.
Have you been having trouble sleeping—like staying up all night thinking about things or sleeping much more than usual even when you don't feel tired?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired a lot, but my sleep itself is pretty normal. I go to bed, I wake up... I'm not staying up all night or anything like that. And I'm not sleeping the whole day away either. It's just a normal amount of sleep, I guess.
Before this current period that started about a year ago, have you ever had an episode where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

No, like I was saying earlier... I really haven't. Before this whole thing started about a year ago, I was doing fine. I didn't have any periods where I felt down or empty like that, not for two weeks or anything.
Since this started about a year ago, have you had any clear periods where you felt significantly better for a while — like a few weeks or more — before feeling down and empty again?

Well, yeah, I guess there was a stretch... maybe for several weeks, where my mood wasn't really all that depressed. I was actually getting through my shifts at work a lot better. But the thing is, even though I felt better mood-wise, I was still hearing that whispering at the condo. And I still felt like I was being watched over my mortgage paperwork.
Before this most recent stretch of feeling better, had you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things before?

No, not before this past year. Like I mentioned a minute ago, before this whole thing started about twelve months back, I was doing fine. I never had any two-week stretches of feeling down or losing interest in things before all this.
Have you ever had a period where you felt so good, full of energy, or restless that it was noticeably different from your usual self—even if it felt good at the time?

No, I haven't. I don't think I've ever had a time where I felt unusually good or... you know, super full of energy like that. Definitely not restless. Even during that stretch I just told you about where my mood was better, I just felt kind of normal, not wired or anything. Waiting tables takes most of my energy anyway, so I've never really had a period where I felt like I had too much of it.
During those periods when you felt better, did you ever feel unusually excited, overly confident, or like you didn’t need as much sleep?

No, I haven't. Like I said, even when my mood picked up, I didn't feel overly excited or anything like that. I didn't feel super confident, and I definitely still needed my sleep. It was just... normal. I wasn't feeling down, but I wasn't bouncing off the walls either.
